title: DiffusionBlocks: Block-wise Neural Network Training via Diffusion Interpretation
claim: Training a network end-to-end needs backprop through every layer; partitioning it into independently trained blocks, each tied to a noise range, removes this and applies across architectures.
layout: 3 panels: left standard network, center DiffusionBlocks blocks, right two stacked application panels; left-to-right with big orange arrow, captions in white boxes
description: The figure has a light-gray background with three regions. On the left, a standard network is drawn as a vertical stack of six gray blocks between input and output boxes. A long blue arrow runs alongside it, labeled "Requires backprop through all layers". A large orange arrow labeled "DiffusionBlocks" points to the middle region. There, the same stack is split into three orange-outlined blocks of two layers each. Each block has its own blue backprop arrow and a plus sign. A min-to-max noise gradient bar sits beside them, with a "noise" label. The caption reads "Train each block independently for specific noise ranges". On the right, two panels show applications. The top panel, Diffusion Models, shows a noisy image turning into a dog photo, with only one block active per step. The bottom panel, Recurrent-depth Models, shows an iterative loop replaced by a single pass. Orange highlights draw the eye first.
caption: Overview of DiffusionBlocks. Left: Standard networks require backpropagation through all layers. Center: DiffusionBlocks partitions networks into blocks, each trained independently to denoise within assigned noise ranges. Right: Applications. For diffusion models (top), inference requires only the relevant block per denoising step. For recurrent-depth models (bottom), our framework replaces iterative training with single-pass training, eliminating the computational overhead of backpropagation through time.
abstract: End-to-end backpropagation requires storing activations throughout all layers, creating memory bottlenecks that limit model scalability. Existing block-wise training methods offer means to alleviate this problem, but they rely on ad-hoc local objectives and remain largely unexplored beyond classification tasks. We propose $\textit{DiffusionBlocks}$, a principled framework for transforming transformer-based networks into genuinely independent trainable blocks that maintain competitive performance with end-to-end training. Our key insight leverages the fact that residual connections naturally correspond to updates in a dynamical system. With minimal modifications to this system, we can convert the updates to those of a denoising process, where each block can be learned independently by leveraging the score matching objective. This independence enables training with gradients for only one block at a time, thereby reducing memory requirements in proportion to the number of blocks. Our experiments on a range of transformer architectures (vision, diffusion, autoregressive, recurrent-depth, and masked diffusion) demonstrate that DiffusionBlocks training matches the performance of end-to-end training while enabling scalable block-wise training on practical tasks beyond small-scale classification. DiffusionBlocks provides a theoretically grounded approach that successfully scales to modern generative tasks across diverse architectures. Code is available at https://github.com/SakanaAI/DiffusionBlocks .
